dedupe_keys.name: isola vicentina municipal water management plan for flood protection veneto italy

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Municipal Water Management Plan of Isola Vicentina in Veneto, Italy, a municipality flooded by the Orolo and Timonchio rivers and, almost every year, by its minor drainage network of reclamation channels, ditches and urban drains during intense rain. Municipal water plans, so far required only in Veneto, coordinate municipalities and land reclamation authorities; the plan combined official river hazard maps and the Eastern Alps flood risk management plan with information from the land reclamation authority, civil protection and residents, who helped identify critical spots in field surveys. It was prepared from October 2015 to June 2016 with IUAV University for 25,000 euro, and planned measures to 2022 include rules for maintaining private ditches, a water retention area and structural works costing about 2 million euro for a 1 in 50 year flood or 4 million euro for 1 in 100 years. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal. Caveats: it is one small municipality, costs are plan estimates, and wider works depend on other authorities. It illustrates local drainage network planning that mixes green retention and grey measures for pluvial flooding; a related record is the EPA National Stormwater Calculator.
name: Isola Vicentina Municipal Water Management Plan for flood protection (Veneto, Italy)
outcomes: A 25,000 euro municipal plan mapped drainage responsibilities and problems and set measures to 2022, with structural options costed at 2 to 4 million euro for 1 in 50 to 1 in 100 year protection.
